projects.title: Did They Really Read?
projects.tagline: Printable fold-and-staple reading journals for any kids' book.
projects.description: Pick a book and how many chapters, and it prints a reading journal your kid can fold and staple. Optional AI writes a question for each chapter, with example answers for the grown-up.
projects.body:
**Did They Really Read?** makes a reading journal for any chapter book: print it double-sided on regular paper, fold it, staple it, and your reader has a journal with a question for every chapter.

It has grown into a library of books with covers, ratings and NYT best-seller history, matched against Open Library and Google Books.
features: Booklet PDF laid out for 8.5x11 paper: print double-sided, fold and staple
Optional AI-written chapter questions with example answers
Book search and cover lookup via Open Library and Google Books
Public book library with ratings and best-seller history
Admin dashboard with usage analytics and a morning email brief

tour.title: Make a journal for any chapter book
tour.text: Search for a book, and the print preview builds right away: a cover, how-to-print instructions and one page per chapter.

tour.title: A question for every chapter
tour.text: Each book has its own page with the chapter count, a sample question and a one-click printable PDF. You can customize the questions or add your reader's name.

tour.title: A library of 360+ ready-made books
tour.text: Browse by series or by what other readers rated highest. Each book has its cover pulled from Open Library and Google Books.

tour.title: Plain pages that print cleanly
tour.text: Every page is black-and-white so it looks right on a home printer. Print double-sided, fold, staple, and it's a booklet.

tour.title: Printable reading logs too
tour.text: Pick what to track (every reading session or every finished book), how many pages, and whether to include a "my favorite part" line.

tour.title: Works from your phone
tour.text: Find a book and send the PDF to the printer from anywhere.

projects.title: Plants
projects.tagline: My plant journal: photo-aware AI chat, care guides and NFC pot tags.
projects.description: A private plant journal where the main screen is a chat. Send a photo or say "watered the monstera" and it updates the real records. Friends can tap the NFC tag on a pot to see how to care for that plant.
projects.body:
The main screen is an AI chat. It recognizes plants from photos and turns what you say into real actions: logging a watering, moving a plant to another room, starting a cutting. Every action can be undone.

Each plant gets a photo timeline, care history and an auto-written care guide, and a **Today** screen shows what needs water. The hardware side: the app generates 3D-printable NFC tag holders, so anyone can tap a pot with their phone and open that plant's public care page.
features: AI chat that identifies plants from photos and logs care actions, with undo
Auto-written care guides and a Today dashboard of watering reminders
Rooms, soil recipes from supplies on hand, cuttings and gifted plants
Public NFC care page for every plant
Generates 3D-printable NFC tag holders (3MF/STL)

projects.title: Lemon Stand Tracker
projects.tagline: A tap-only order and profit tracker for kid-run lemonade stands.
projects.description: A simple tracker that lets kids run their own lemonade stand: big tap buttons for orders, recipe steps for making drinks, help with making change, and a report at the end that shows whether they made money.
projects.body:
Most POS apps are far too complicated for a kid-run stand. This one keeps it to big tap buttons, recipe steps for making drinks, and help with making change. It also shows the business side: what the cups and lemons cost, what sold, and whether the stand made a profit.

Supplies are subtracted automatically with every cup sold. **Kid Mode** hides the settings and costs, so the kids can run the stand themselves.
features: Tap-only order screen with a cash change calculator and Venmo/Cash App QR codes
Make queue with recipe steps
Supplies auto-deducted per order, with cost per cup and profit
Daily report: revenue, tips, margin, best sellers, CSV export
Kid Mode hides settings, costs and delete buttons

projects.title: Fitness Field Notes
projects.tagline: A no-nonsense digital gym notebook for lifters.
projects.description: A minimalist workout log: build templates and multi-week programs, track sessions live, and review your history and PRs. No social feed, no gamification, and no account required.
projects.body:
This is the latest version of a gym logger I keep rebuilding (see the [Gym Workout Logger](/projects/gym-workout-logger.html), which started as a Word template filler). I wanted the simplicity of a paper notebook with the advantages of an app.

You can paste a workout as plain text, a PDF, a spreadsheet or even a photo, and AI turns it into a structured workout.
features: Workout builder and multi-week program manager
Live session tracking with history and personal records
AI import from plain text, PDF, CSV or a photo
Exercise database with GIF demos
Works without an account (browser storage)

tour.title: A gym notebook, not a social network
tour.text: Write down what you did and see your progress over time. No feeds, no streaks, and no account needed to start.

tour.title: Build workouts in the Workout Studio
tour.text: Search 1,600+ exercises by name, muscle or equipment and tap to add them, then organize them into a workout or a multi-week program.

tour.title: Every exercise explained
tour.text: Each exercise has a demo and step-by-step instructions, and you can favorite the ones you use.

tour.title: Borrow a workout from the community
tour.text: Browse workouts other lifters have shared, filtered by push, pull, legs, full body and more, and save them to your own library.

tour.title: Made for the gym floor
tour.text: The whole thing works on your phone, with a Log Session button always in reach.

projects.title: Baseball Board
projects.tagline: An animated tactics board for coaching: drag players, then play the sequence.
projects.description: A whiteboard for baseball coaches: drag fielders, runners and the ball around the diamond, save each position as a step, then play it back as an animation. It covers cutoffs, rundowns, double plays and base coverage.
projects.body:
Set up a play step by step (cutoffs, rundowns, double plays, base coverage), then **play it back** so everyone can see who moves where.

It includes a library of scenarios organized by position, and it's built to work on a phone at the field.
features: Draggable defenders, runners and ball on a top-down field
Step-by-step timeline with animated playback and speed control
Scenario library organized by position
Focus mode and phone-friendly controls
Plays saved in the browser

projects.title: Who's More Tan?
projects.tagline: Put your arms together and let your phone camera decide who's more tan.
projects.description: A silly camera app for settling summer arguments. Two people put their arms side by side, and the app samples both, corrects for the lighting, and picks a winner over best of three. Photos never leave your phone.
projects.body:
A fun color-science project. The app compares skin tones in the CIELAB color space, filters out glare and shadows, and can use a white card as a lighting reference.

It's purely for entertainment, and all processing happens in your browser.
features: Live camera capture with upload fallback
Draggable sampling circles and an optional white-balance card
CIELAB color comparison that filters out glare and shadows
Best-of-three rounds with a shareable result card
Installable PWA; photos never leave the device

projects.title: ContactCapture
projects.tagline: Paste any messy text and AI turns it into a contact in Outlook or Google.
projects.description: Paste an email signature, a LinkedIn blurb or business-card text, and AI extracts a clean contact. Review it, then save it to Outlook and/or Google Contacts with one click.
projects.body: Paste whatever you have (an email signature, a LinkedIn blurb, business-card text), check the fields it extracted, and save. There's no retyping.
projects.waitlistPitch: ContactCapture is an MVP right now. If you’d use it with your Outlook or Google account, leave your email and I’ll let you know when it opens up.
features: AI extracts structured contact fields from any text
One-click save to Outlook (Microsoft 365) and/or Google Contacts
Sign in with Microsoft or Google
History of captured contacts

projects.title: Red Sox vs Yankees Beer Series
projects.tagline: Settling a six-pack-per-series bet with the MLB Stats API.
projects.description: A six-pack is on the line every Red Sox-Yankees series. This site pulls the games from the MLB Stats API, groups them into series, decides each winner, and tracks who still owes beer.
features: Live game data from the MLB Stats API
Series winner as soon as it's clinched; splits owe nothing
Dashboard, schedule and calendar views
Season history with a Paid/Unpaid toggle
